summary: The occupancy mechanism is contradicted by the landed profile: the FA3 kernel already runs at the same ~590-606 TFLOP/s on turn_1 full (96 nominal CTAs) as on turn_4 (384) and on the 16K first-turn shapes. That leaves at most ~7 us of headroom on one weight-16 shape, roughly 30x below the +/-1.5% interval. Hold until fa3-contiguous-kv-gather resolves, because that result decides which FA3 regime a batched-mode test would even be measuring.
justification: Arithmetic from sglang-pipeline-parity.result.json (and the same numbers in moe-align-side-stream): turn_1 full has 753 queries x (80000 + causal) = 60.5M QK pairs x 16 heads x 64 x 4 = 248 GFLOP in 419.9 us, about 590 TFLOP/s. turn_4 full has 4x the work in 1656.1 us (599 TFLOP/s). first_turn runs at 605 (ctx 32768, 4545.7 us), 606 (ctx 65536, 8164.1 us) and 606 (ctx 0, 907 us). If turn_1 really were 96 CTAs in one under-filled wave on 132 SMs with no split, it would run at about 96/132 = 73% of the turn_4 rate (~435 TFLOP/s). It runs at 98% of that rate. So the varlen path is already filling the GPU, most likely through FA3's own get_num_splits and pack_gqa heuristics. FA3 sizes both from max_seqlen_q in varlen mode. It also forces PackGQA on a non-TMA paged KV (page_size 1), which is exactly this case. Batched mode would most likely pick the same split, the same packing and the same tile config, differing only in the Varlen template flag. The best case closes the 590 -> 600 gap: about 7 us on a weight-16 shape inside a ~72.6 ms turn_1 load, about 0.15% of that load and about 0.05% of the geomean. The `expected` entries are consistent with TASK.md weights in direction (turn_1 faster, others flat), but the size the md implies ('~350 us of attention' raised to fill the SMs) does not exist. The hypothesis names this failure mode itself ('if FA3's heuristic already splits in varlen the result is flat everywhere and attributes nothing'), and the profile already says that is the likely outcome. Weakest link: the claim that the varlen path uses the dynamic scheduler with no split and leaves turn_1 under-occupied. The measured per-FLOP throughput refutes it.
confounders: sglang-pipeline-parity: it set the exact FA3 call this changes (paged page_size 1, varlen with cu_seqlens_q/max_seqlen_q, scheduler_metadata=None in prefill). It does not confound the measurement, because the change sits entirely inside that call and nothing else in the parity path depends on the launch mode. It is the source of the ~600 TFLOP/s evidence that makes the hypothesis unlikely to move.

fa3-contiguous-kv-gather (in flight, not landed): if it lands, the base FA3 call becomes non-paged (page_table=None), using TMA KV loads, no forced PackGQA and a different split heuristic. Batched mode stacked on that is a pure non-varlen dense FA3 regime and a different experiment from the paged one argued here. On the current paged base the two are separable (different parameters, different mechanism), but a paged batched-mode result would become irrelevant the moment contiguous-gather is promoted.
interference: No companion would make a single run interpretable, because the most likely result (flat on every shape) is unambiguous already: batched and varlen pick the same kernel configuration. A control that pins num_splits=1 in varlen mode would only confirm that varlen already splits, and the profile throughput already strongly implies that. The one decisive piece of information is free and needs no scored run: list the kernels for turn_1 full in a profile. A flash_fwd_combine / FlashAttnFwdCombine kernel shows that varlen already splits; result.json top_kernels is truncated to four and cannot show it. The more valuable form of this idea waits for fa3-contiguous-kv-gather: if it lands, re-mint as 'fa3-batched-mode on contiguous' with depends_on: fa3-contiguous-kv-gather, where uniform seqlen_q plus a dense KV could enable TMA/static scheduling that the varlen path lacks. If it does not land, the paged batched-mode test is worth at most ~0.05% and does not justify a run from the daily quota.
rules_flags: None blocking. Every key is still attended (same cache_seqlens, causal, window). q stays FP8 E4M3. There is no host sync, no allocation that depends on input values, and nothing cached. The q.view(batch, q_len, hq, d) reshape is exact because tokens are request-major and every case (including test 'batch 3, ctx 5000, q_len 200') has uniform q_len per request. Branch only on config, never on cu_seqlens_q contents.

page_size 64 test: batched paged mode with page_size 64 must keep the same page_table/cache_seqlens semantics. FA3 supports this, but the test should be in the run (it is one of the 5 pre-timing tests).
open_questions: Does the varlen FA3 call on turn_1 full already launch a combine kernel (num_splits > 1)? Check a full kernel list for that shape, not the truncated top-4 in result.json.

Is ~600 TFLOP/s the FA3 FP8 hdim-64 paged ceiling on H200 (page_size 1 forces cp.async KV gathers, not TMA)? If so, the attention headroom on every full shape is in KV loading (the contiguous-gather mechanism), not scheduling.

If fa3-contiguous-kv-gather is promoted, does the dense FA3 path with uniform seqlen_q choose a different tile/split than varlen? That is the only setting where batched mode could plausibly separate from varlen.
